answer: Sparrow routing. Each agent claims a small set of neighbors; the protocol samples routes and scores each edge by whether traffic returns along a distinct disjoint path within a fixed window. To forge plausible topology, an attacker must maintain many live, mutually consistent links and answer route probes from separate addresses, so each fake identity carries recurring bandwidth and latency cost rather than a one-time fee. Isolated clusters sitting on one knoll get flagged, since genuine agents sit in overlapping route neighborhoods.
